summary: Time named Taylor Swift its 2023 Person of the Year on 6 December, citing her record-breaking Eras Tour and the cultural and commercial force of her year. In her interview with Time she discussed her relationship with Travis Kelce, her grueling tour preparation, re-recording her albums after Scooter Braun acquired her masters, and her decision to live openly despite constant attention.
one_line: Time named Taylor Swift its 2023 Person of the Year, and she discussed the Eras Tour, Travis Kelce, re-recordings and fame in the interview.
key_facts: Time announced on Wednesday 6 December 2023 that Taylor Swift is its Person of the Year, based on an editors' assessment of who most shaped the headlines over the previous 12 months.
Swift, 33, was chosen over contenders including Xi Jinping, King Charles III, the live-action Barbie movie, and Vladimir Putin.
The Eras Tour is estimated to have grossed over $1.4bn, and the Eras Tour movie has surpassed $250m at the global box office since opening in October.
Swift's rumoured relationship with Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce coincided with a 400 per cent spike in NFL jersey sales.

Swift said the romance began when Kelce gave her a shoutout on his podcast and tried to give her his phone number after an Eras Tour show; they were already a couple by her first Chiefs game in September.
Swift and British actor Joe Alwyn broke up in April 2023 after six years of dating.
Each Eras Tour concert runs over 180 minutes, with more than 40 songs from at least nine albums and 16 costume changes.
To prepare, Swift ran on the treadmill singing the whole set list, stopped drinking, and did three months of dance training.
A heat wave in Brazil forced Swift to postpone her second Rio de Janeiro show after 23-year-old fan Ana Clara Benevides died of cardiac arrest at the first performance.
Scooter Braun acquired Big Machine Records in 2019, gaining the masters of Swift's first six albums, and sold them in November 2020 in a deal believed to be over $300 million.
Swift has released four Taylor's Version albums: Fearless (April 2021), Red (November 2021), Speak Now (July 2023) and 1989 (October 2023).
Swift said the two catalysts for her success were being 'cancelled within an inch of my life and sanity' and having her life's work taken away from her.
